In the government school at Kudur village, Sangeeta arrived on Monday with a new school bag: bright blue, with a zip pocket and a picture of a kite. Lakshmi's own bag was her brother's old cloth one, the strap tied in a knot.
All morning Lakshmi kept glancing at the blue bag. At lunch under the neem tree, she told the other girls loudly, "Sangeeta is only showing off. She's jealous of everyone, that's why she wants us all to look."
Sangeeta, who had only put her bag on the bench, looked down at her rice.
Walking home along the canal, Lakshmi kicked a stone the whole way and didn't say why.

qa.a: A picture of a kite.

qa.q: Why does Lakshmi call Sangeeta jealous?
qa.a: Lakshmi longs for a bag like that, but calling Sangeeta the jealous one lets her avoid seeing the envy in herself.

qa.q: What could Lakshmi try the next time she wants what someone else has?
qa.a: Noticing the pang and saying it honestly, even just to herself or a friend, like 'I wish I had a bag like that', instead of blaming Sangeeta.

qa.q: What is lunch like for Sangeeta after Lakshmi's words?
qa.a: Sangeeta probably feels embarrassed and confused, since she only put her bag down and suddenly everyone is looking 😔

At recess he told his friend Mateo, "Layla's such a show-off. She's jealous of everybody, that's why she has to have the best stuff."
Mateo frowned. "She didn't even say anything about it."
"Exactly," Diego said, which didn't quite make sense. That night he asked his mom how much light-up backpacks cost, then said, "Never mind. They're dumb anyway."

On the first day after the holidays, Sudha walked into the Class 6 library period with a shiny new satchel her aunt had sent. Mohit, eleven, slid lower in his chair. He had been asking for a new bag for a year.
When the librarian told everyone to put their bags on the rack, Mohit said, loud enough for the whole table, "Some people just love showing off. Sudha's jealous of everyone, that's why she needs us all to look at her."
Sudha went pink and pushed her satchel to the back of the rack.
The librarian looked up. "Mohit, that's a strong thing to say. What made you think of it?"
Mohit opened his mouth, shut it, and stared at the satchel a second too long.

qa.a: Her aunt.

qa.q: Why does Mohit stare at the satchel a second too long?
qa.a: He seems to want it badly, having asked for a new bag for a year; calling Sudha jealous covers the envy he can't face in himself.

qa.q: What did the librarian's question give Mohit a chance to do?
qa.a: It gave Mohit a pause to notice where his words came from, instead of just being told off; a quiet follow-up could help him name the envy.

qa.q: What is the library period like for Sudha after Mohit's comment?
qa.a: Sudha likely feels embarrassed and singled out, hiding a gift she was probably happy about.

grounding: In a school library an eleven-year-old boy who has wanted a new bag for a year accuses a classmate with a new satchel of jealousy.
